name: Dorsal column - medial lemniscus (body)
modality: Conscious proprioception, fine touch, vibration, pressure, skin stretch

neurons.tract: fasciculus gracilis (legs, below T6; sacral fibres most medial) / fasciculus cuneatus (arms, above T6; cervical fibres lateral), dorsal funiculus; enter by the medial DREZ
internal arcuate fibers then medial lemniscus (topography kept; trigeminal lemniscus joins it from the face)

name: Anterolateral spinothalamic pathway (body)

neurons.tract: A-delta and C fibers, lateral dorsal root entry zone
neurons.synapse: marginal zone (A-delta) / substantia gelatinosa onto nucleus proprius (C), ipsilateral

neurons.cell_body: marginal zone nucleus (sharp pain) or nucleus proprius (dull pain)
neurons.tract: anterior (ventral) white commissure then contralateral anterolateral tract in the anterior/lateral funiculi; collaterals to brainstem pain centres (reticular formation, periaqueductal grey)

decussation: Spinal cord (anterior white commissure), near the level of entry

lesion.below_decussation: ipsilateral loss limited to the level of the lesion (fibres not yet crossed)

neurons.tract: A-alpha (Ia/Ib) from muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs, medial DREZ
dorsal spinocerebellar tract (lateral funiculus), inferior cerebellar peduncle

neurons.cell_body: brainstem nuclei (Edinger-Westphal for CN III, superior salivatory for VII, inferior salivatory for IX, dorsal motor nucleus of X) or lateral horn S2-S4
neurons.synapse: ganglion near or in the target organ

name: Upper and lower motor neuron hierarchy

neurons.synapse: LMN in ventral horn or brainstem motor nucleus

name: Trigeminal discriminative touch (face)
modality: Fine touch, vibration, pressure from the face

neurons.synapse: principal sensory nucleus of V, ipsilateral

name: Trigeminal pain and temperature (face)
modality: Pain, temperature, itch, crude touch from the head: CN V (face, eye, nasal cavity, oral cavity, meninges), VII (small area near the ear), IX (oropharynx, middle ear), X (laryngopharynx, esophagus below the epiglottis)

neurons.cell_body: trigeminal ganglion (CN V); CN VII, IX and X afferents also end in the spinal trigeminal nucleus

decussation: Brainstem, just after the spinal trigeminal nucleus

neurons.cell_body: mesencephalic nucleus of V (inside the CNS)
layer V pyramidal neurons, primary motor cortex
neurons.tract: corona radiata, internal capsule, cerebral peduncle, longitudinal pontine fibers, pyramid, lateral corticospinal tract
neurons.synapse: lateral ventral horn LMNs (limb), ipsilateral to the tract

neurons.cell_body: alpha motor neuron, lateral ventral horn

name: Anterior corticospinal tract

neurons.cell_body: layer V pyramidal neurons (trunk motor cortex)
alpha motor neuron, medial ventral horn
neurons.level: medial ventral horn, both sides (axial / trunk)

decussation: No decussation in the medulla; bilateral termination

name: Corticobulbar (corticonuclear) pathway
modality: Voluntary movement of face, jaw, tongue, pharynx

neurons.cell_body: layer V neurons, lateral motor cortex
neurons.tract: corona radiata, internal capsule genu, cerebral peduncle
neurons.synapse: cranial motor nuclei (V, VII, ambiguus, XII); some fibres end in the red nucleus and reticular formation
neurons.level: axons cross just above each nucleus

decussation: Just superior to each motor nucleus

name: Corticopontocerebellar pathway
modality: Cortical motor plan to the cerebellum

neurons.tract: transverse pontine fibers, middle cerebellar peduncle

name: Rubrospinal tract
modality: Brainstem UMN pathway: flexion of the contralateral upper limb

neurons.tract: rubrospinal: brainstem tegmentum, then lateral funiculus beside the lateral corticospinal tract
neurons.synapse: lower motor neurons of the contralateral upper limb (flexion)

decussation: Crosses to the contralateral side (projects to the contralateral upper limb); the level of crossing is not named in the slides

name: Tectospinal tract
modality: Brainstem UMN pathway: turning head toward visual and auditory stimuli

neurons.synapse: lower motor neurons at cervical and upper thoracic levels (neck and upper trunk muscles)

name: Reticulospinal tracts
modality: Brainstem UMN pathway: posture, stepping; pontine facilitates extensors, medullary inhibits

neurons.tract: reticulospinal (pontine and medullary tracts), anterior (ventral) funiculus
neurons.synapse: lower motor neurons in the ventral horn

name: Vestibulospinal tract
modality: Brainstem UMN pathway: posture and balance, righting reflexes

neurons.synapse: lower motor neurons in the ventral horn for axial muscles

neurons.cell_body: bipolar cell (first-order); rods and cones are the receptors

neurons.tract: optic nerve, optic chiasm (nasal fibers cross), optic tract; branches also reach the suprachiasmatic nucleus (circadian rhythm) and the superior colliculus / pretectal nucleus (visual reflexes)

neurons.level: occipital lobe; retinotopic map kept (upper field in inferior V1, lower field in superior V1)

lesion.below_decussation: optic nerve: loss of sight in that eye; optic chiasm: tunnel vision (loss of peripheral vision in each eye)
lesion.above: optic tract onward: loss of the opposite visual field in both eyes (homonymous); primary visual cortex: hemianopia or quadrantopia, with or without macular sparing

name: Pupillary light reflex

neurons.tract: CN II to the pretectal nucleus (near the superior colliculus), then to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei
neurons.synapse: CN III parasympathetics to the ciliary ganglion, then sphincter pupillae (the same pathway constricts the pupil in accommodation)

decussation: Light in one eye reaches both Edinger-Westphal nuclei (consensual reflex); no named commissure in the slides

neurons.synapse: spinal trigeminal nucleus then bilateral facial nuclei

lesion.below_decussation: afferent CN V lesion: no blink either eye
lesion.above: efferent CN VII lesion: no blink on that side

name: Horizontal conjugate gaze

neurons.synapse: abducens nucleus, then MLF to contralateral oculomotor nucleus

decussation: FEF fibers cross to the contralateral PPRF

lesion.below_decussation: MLF lesion: disconjugate gaze (the eye on the lesion side cannot adduct on lateral gaze; convergence is intact)
lesion.above: FEF lesion: eyes deviate to the lesion side (derived from: right FEF drives the eyes left)

name: Cerebellar circuit (motor comparator)

neurons.cell_body: mossy: pontine nuclei (contra, MCP), DSCT (ipsi, ICP), vestibular (ipsi); climbing: inferior olive (contra, ICP)

neurons.synapse: contralateral red nucleus and VA/VL thalamus (then motor cortex); also brainstem UMN groups (vestibular nucleus, reticular formation)

decussation: Caudal midbrain (decussation of the superior cerebellar peduncle)

neurons.tract: striatopallidal: direct 'go' (striatum inhibits GPi, which disinhibits the thalamus) and indirect 'no-go' (striatum inhibits GPe, which disinhibits the STN; STN drives GPi); substantia nigra pars compacta dopamine: D1 excites direct, D2 inhibits indirect

lesion.above: hyperkinesia (STN lesion: ballismus; striatal degeneration: Huntington chorea) or hypokinesia (loss of nigral dopamine: Parkinson, bradykinesia)

name: Olfactory pathway

neurons.tract: CN I through the cribriform plate
olfactory tract (bypasses the thalamus for the first relay)
neurons.synapse: olfactory tubercle and prepiriform cortex (awareness of smell); MD thalamus to orbitofrontal cortex (discrimination); hypothalamus and limbic areas via entorhinal cortex and hippocampus

decussation: None in the main pathway (bypasses the thalamus)

neurons.synapse: mammillary bodies, septal nuclei, basal forebrain

name: Auditory (cochlear) pathway

neurons.synapse: inferior colliculus (auditory reflexes: turning to a noise)

neurons.tract: relays up the brainstem to the thalamus
neurons.synapse: medial geniculate nucleus of the thalamus
primary auditory cortex (BA 41, 42, transverse temporal gyrus)

decussation: Not taught in the slides (lecture 8: be familiar with the structures, do not memorize the whole pathway)

name: Vestibular pathways
modality: Head position and acceleration (semicircular canals: rotation; utricle and saccule: gravity, linear acceleration)

neurons.tract: ascending to thalamus and cortex; ascending MLF to CN III, IV, VI nuclei; descending MLF to the cervical cord; vestibulospinal tract
neurons.synapse: thalamus (conscious perception of movement); eye-movement nuclei (vestibulo-ocular reflex, eyes move opposite to the head); cervical cord; ventral horn trunk muscles (righting)

name: Stretch reflex (monosynaptic)
modality: Muscle length: spindle (Ia) afferent drives the alpha motor neuron, no interneuron (knee jerk, L3/L4)

neurons.cell_body: dorsal root ganglion (pseudounipolar, muscle spindle Ia afferent)
neurons.synapse: alpha motor neuron in the ventral horn, directly
neurons.level: spinal segment of entry (knee jerk: L3/L4)

name: Withdrawal reflex (polysynaptic)
modality: Skin stimulus (e.g. touching something hot) withdraws the limb through spinal interneurons

neurons.synapse: interneuron(s) in the dorsal / ventral horn

neurons.tract: local spinal circuit (open to descending modulation)
neurons.synapse: alpha motor neuron in the ventral horn

name: Solitary nucleus: taste and visceral reflexes
modality: Taste (special sensory) and visceral sensation (baroreceptors, chemoreceptors, GI stretch) from CN VII, IX, X

neurons.cell_body: peripheral ganglion of CN VII, IX or X (cell bodies outside the brainstem)
neurons.tract: cranial nerve to the solitary tract
neurons.synapse: solitary nucleus: rostral part for taste, caudal part for cardiovascular, respiratory and GI input
superior and inferior salivatory nuclei, dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus, nucleus ambiguus, lateral horn T1-L2
